newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks mixed as JSE turnover hits record.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks mixed as JSE turnover hits record.

text.p: South African shares ended mixed on Wednesday, but an enormous asset swap deal by broker SBC Warburg boosted turnover into record territory, dealers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) said.

The asset swap, which dealers said probably represented a portfolio being moved offshore, lifted overall trading value to 2.776 billion rands worth of shares -- beating the previous April 29 record of 2.171 billion rand.

A Warburg spokesman confirmed the trades had taken place involving most major blue-chip shares, but declined to give further details. Dealers at other brokerages said Warburg's deal had covered about two billion rands worth of the day's trade.

The huge volumes in major shares provided a firm tone for the market, which had been expected to head downwards, bullied by futures traders rushing to settle positions ahead of Friday's contracts close-out.
The all-share index ended up 26.3 points to 7,218.4 as industrials dropped just 0.6 points to 8,432.1.

Among individual shares Gencor added 165 cents to end at 20.75 rand after news of a spin-off of its Billiton base metals operation to list in London and plans to raise more than $1 billion overseas. The firm also sealed a nickel merger deal with Australia's QNI Ltd.

The gold market was stranded by little real interest. The share index ended down 3.8 points at 1,096.7. Dealers said shares were suffering from a bleak outlook on the prospects for the bullion price that emerged from a recent gold conference in Prague.
